heroHeadline: Day 764: Sinaloa Names Second Interim Governor of 2026 — Graciela Domínguez Nava Sworn In (Aug 25) After Rocha Moya's 34-Hour Return Ends in New Indefinite Leave; SEDENA Surges 1,300 More Troops to Mazatlán
heroSubtitle: 764 days of cartel civil war — through August 26, 2026: Sinaloa's political crisis deepened after Governor Rubén Rocha Moya's August 21 return to office lasted only 34 hours before he filed a second, indefinite leave request on August 22 amid renewed pressure from within his own Morena party and the unresolved SDNY drug-trafficking indictment against him. The state Congress approved the leave August 23 and, on August 25, voted 36-4 to install Graciela Domínguez Nava — Rocha Moya's former Secretary of Public Education and Culture — as Sinaloa's second interim governor of 2026, serving through October 31, 2027; President Sheinbaum said she learned of the appointment during her own morning press conference and pledged federal coordination on security. Domínguez immediately convened her first Cabinet meeting, pledging 'nuestra prioridad será la paz' and promising a governance-and-security plan the following week. The federal government moved in parallel to reinforce the state: SEDENA airlifted 300 troops to Mazatlán on August 25, followed by roughly 1,000 more on August 26 — a two-day, 1,300-troop surge under the National Public Security Strategy that pushes Sinaloa's cumulative federal deployment above 14,000, the largest concentrated military footprint of any Mexican state. Statewide violence continues unabated: July 2026 closed as the deadliest month of the year for women (12 femicide investigations) and the second-deadliest overall (138 violent deaths), while La Mayiza continues to hold roughly 90% territorial control under a four-faction fragmented cartel structure (International Crisis Group, July 7).
